name: three-body

VINIT.justification: The uninitialized 18-dimensional phase space before mass injection or coordinate assignment.

TANCH.justification: The terminal constraint where the determinant of the flow Jacobian must equal unity to preserve phase space volume.

AFWD.justification: The forward directed transformation of the state vector through time using fourth-order composition.

AREV.justification: The contravariant transformation that reverses the velocity vector to test numerical reversibility.

CLINK.justification: The composition of multiple integration steps into a continuous trajectory segment.

IMSCRIB.justification: The identity check where the system recognizes its own energy and angular momentum as invariant constants.

FSPLIT.justification: The bifurcation of the absolute state into a center-of-mass arm and a relative-motion arm.

FFUSE.justification: The reconstitution of absolute Cartesian coordinates from the center-of-mass and relative components.

EVALT.justification: The affirmative evaluation of a stable trajectory residing on a KAM torus.

EVALF.justification: The negative evaluation indicating chaotic divergence and sensitive dependence on initial conditions.

ENGAGR.justification: The simultaneous holding of stable and chaotic states at the edge of the resonance manifold.

IFIX.justification: The permanent irreversible fixation of state crossings on a lower-dimensional transverse surface.

phase_3.void_description: uninitialized phase space with zero mass and zero momentum
phase_3.true_description: integrable motion characterized by uniform rotation numbers and stable tori
phase_3.false_description: chaotic motion characterized by positive Lyapunov exponents and orbital divergence
phase_3.both_description: mixed phase space where stable islands and chaotic seas coexist at the KAM boundary

steps.domain_action: initialize the 18-dimensional phase space vector to zero
load figure-eight initial conditions and verify initial energy conservation
propagate the system forward by one orbital period using symplectic integration
decompose the absolute state into barycentric and relative Jacobi coordinates
propagate the barycentric arm analytically as a free particle
verify the relative arm exhibits quasi-periodic rotation numbers
perform a momentum-flip to benchmark the numerical reversibility of the integration
calculate the Fast Lyapunov Indicator to ensure the initial orbit is not chaotic
reconstruct the absolute Cartesian state from the Jacobi components
apply a velocity perturbation to push the system toward the KAM stability boundary
chain ten thousand symplectic steps to observe long-term orbital evolution
record state crossings on the y-axis to generate a permanent Poincaré section
verify that total energy and angular momentum remain invariant after long-term integration
compute the flow Jacobian determinant to confirm Liouville volume preservation

phase_6.cycle_cost: numerical round-off error and floating-point drift
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the symplectic integrator preserves the wedge product and Liouville volume
